questions.q: What question does an account rule answer?
options: Whether a journal line should be a debit or credit
Which GL account, or which segment of a GL account, a specific journal line should post to
Whether an invoice has been paid
How many days until an invoice is due
questions.explain: Account rules derive the GL account (or a specific segment) that a journal line should use; journal line rules, by contrast, decide whether the line exists and its debit/credit nature.

questions.q: A rule that always assigns the exact same Cost Center value, no matter what the transaction looks like, is using which kind of value?
options: A mapping set
A source value
A constant value
A priority override
questions.explain: A constant value always returns the same fixed result regardless of the transaction's data.

questions.q: What is the purpose of priority order within an account rule?
options: It determines how fast the rule executes
It resolves which value assignment wins when more than one condition could apply, by evaluating conditions in order and using the first match
It decides which subledger application runs first
It controls which currency is used
questions.explain: When multiple conditions could match a transaction, priority order determines which one actually applies, in sequence, stopping at the first match.

questions.q: What is the difference between an account rule built per segment and an account combination rule?
options: There is no real difference; they are the same object with two names
An account rule per segment derives one piece of the account (like just the Cost Center), while an account combination rule derives the entire account string in one step
Account combination rules can only be used in Receivables
Account rules per segment can never use source values
questions.explain: Building rules per segment is the common, flexible approach; an account combination rule instead derives the whole account in a single step, often from a source account.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of using a source value in an account rule?
options: Always hardcoding Cost Center 999 regardless of the transaction
Pulling the natural account directly from the AP invoice distribution already recorded on the transaction
Looking up a value in a translation table with multiple inputs
Ignoring the transaction entirely and leaving the segment blank
questions.explain: A source value takes data directly from the originating transaction, such as the natural account already present on the invoice distribution.
